title: InkEvent
description: Every event the Inkwell core sends a shell through the C ABI (core/crates/ink-ffi/include/inkwell.h): one JSON object, its kind in "type". The Swift types in mac/ are generated from this file by `cargo run -p ink-ffi --bin ink-schema`; the generator reads a subset of JSON Schema (string enums, objects of scalars, arrays and references) and refuses anything else. Optional fields are omitted, never null.

Channel.description: A side of a meeting: the mic is you, the far end is them (stream identity, architecture rule 5).

EngineSource.description: Where a routed engine comes from: registry (a model downloaded from the built-in registry) or shell (an engine the shell registered, such as FluidAudio's Parakeet on the Mac).

EngineKind.description: What kind of engine the shell registered: offline (finals), streaming (live partials) or llm (a language model, for dictation polish).

Job.description: A job the router fills with the best installed engine.

VadUnavailable.description: Why no voice detection model is in use.

FailureCode.description: A command.failed a shell acts on. list_unreadable: a snippets.save, voice_commands.save, meetings.calls.set, modes.save or modes.delete refused because the stored list cannot be read (send a save again with replace_unreadable to start over). meeting_recording: an audio.test refused because a meeting records: the mic test waits until it ends. delete_window_over: a meeting.discard after the meeting's first minute: only Stop is left, and the record can be deleted from the library once it is finished. For modes.save and modes.delete: name_blank (a mode needs a name), name_taken (another mode's name sounds the same: case and spacing aside), name_is_style (formal, casual and relaxed are the styles' names in voice commands), too_long (a name over 64 characters, polish instructions over 2,000, more than 64 apps in a mode or an app identity over 256 characters, or more than 50 modes; a mode the 0.2 import brought with more than 64 apps saves a change to its apps only once they are 64 or fewer, so the editor says "Shorten to 64 apps or fewer."), default_mode (the default mode can't be deleted or given apps), app_taken (an app the mode is given is another mode's: send the save again with take_apps to move it), mode_not_found (no mode has that id) model_unknown (no language model the core holds has that id: modes.listed lists them), model_name_invalid (a polish_model_name that is over 128 characters or holds a control character, or one given for a model that is not a provider's, or without a model), destination_changed (a polish_model_confirm whose model sends somewhere else now than its polish_model_confirm_to, the destination the user agreed to: list the modes again and ask again; nothing was saved) and app_invalid (an app identity with a control character, of one character, or with no letter: as a substring of the frontmost app's identity it would match nearly every app).

Refusal.description: Why a job's model was refused.

Discard.description: Why a dictation ended without an insertion. None of these is an error.

CommandAction.description: A voice command. The core carries out change_style, toggle_polish and insert_text itself; the others are recognised and not carried out in this build.

Risk.description: How much confirmation a voice command needs: safe runs at once, moderate gets a brief notice the user can cancel, dangerous asks first.

InsertOutcome.description: How a dictation went in. blocked: Secure Input or an elevated target refused synthetic input, and nothing was inserted. inserted_clipboard_not_restored: inserted, and the previous clipboard could not be put back.

FailedStage.description: Which stage of a dictation failed.

DictationWarning.description: Something went wrong during a dictation, and it went on without it. deleted_text_not_scrubbed and deleted_text_scrubbed: as for meetings. release_missed: a push-to-talk key was held for 180 s with no release (most likely lost); the take was stopped there and processed. polish_not_allowed: polish is on, but the user has not agreed to send dictations where its model goes now (never agreed, or the model changed destination since): nothing was sent, the text went in as said, and message names the model; consent.get says more. polish_model_missing: polish is on for this mode, and the mode names a language model of its own that the core does not hold now (let go of, or another provider chosen in Settings > AI): nothing was sent anywhere and the text went in as said; polish never falls back to another model.

SideState.description: What a meeting side is delivering, as the silent-channel watchdog judges it: ok, stopped (no audio where it must keep coming), zeros (only exact zeros: no data at all, most often a denied capture).

Phase.description: Which part of a meeting a problem came from.

MeetingWarning.description: Something went wrong in a meeting, and it went on without it. deleted_text_not_scrubbed: text the library deleted or replaced could not yet be cleared from its files (another process is reading the database; the change is saved, and the store keeps trying); deleted_text_scrubbed: it now is. Each is sent once per change. not_crash_protected: the crash-recovery marker could not be written when the meeting started, so if the app quits unexpectedly this meeting is not finished at the next launch (its audio is still saved). summary_not_allowed: the user has not agreed to send meeting transcripts where the language model goes now (the meetings consent: never agreed, or the model changed destination since): nothing was sent, so the meeting has no summary and no commitments, and message names the model; consent.get says more.

KeptLive.description: Why the final pass did not replace the live transcript: refused (the supersede guard: an empty result, or a side under half its live words) or incomplete (some regions failed).

JobScore.description: An engine's measured word error rate on one job.

ChannelPass.description: What a meeting's final pass did on one side.

chunks_written.description: Chunk files the pump wrote for this side; absent when the pump did not report.

chunks.description: Chunk files the final pass found.

captured_ms.description: Audio in the readable chunks, ms. Zero: nothing was captured.

backlogged_finals.description: Live finals saved without the speech check.

audible_ms.description: Time above the audible floor, ms, before any gain.

regions.description: Speech regions the engine was given.

empty_regions.description: Regions that came back without words.

speech_ms.description: Time the VAD found as speech, ms.

CoreReady.description: The core started. The first event after ink_init.

abi.description: The core's ABI version; must equal INK_ABI_VERSION in inkwell.h.

CoreStopped.description: The last event before ink_shutdown returns.

CommandFailed.description: A command was read and could not be carried out.

id.description: The command's "id", when it had one.

message.description: Why. Names what failed, never what was said.

code.description: Which failure, for the few a shell acts on; absent for the rest. Match on this, never on the message.

EngineRegistered.description: An engine the shell registered is in use: an offline or streaming engine in the router, or a language model for polish.

kind.description: What kind of engine it is.

jobs.description: The jobs it fills; empty for a language model.

items.description: A job and its error rate.

EngineRouted.description: What serves a job now, in answer to engine.route: the router's choice among installed models and registered engines. Without id, nothing installed or registered fills the job.

id.description: The engine that serves it: a registry model's id, or the id a shell engine registered under.

EngineUnregistered.description: An engine the shell registered was let go; its release function runs once no call is in flight.

ModelWarmed.description: A job's model is loaded and kept loaded.

ModelWarmFailed.description: A job's model could not be warmed.

id.description: The model's id, when one was chosen.

ModelRefused.description: A job asked for a model that is held exclusively (being updated), and was refused. The job fails; nothing was loaded from files being replaced.

ModelUpdateStarted.description: A model update holds its model: jobs that need it are refused until model.update_finished.

ModelUpdateProgress.description: How far a model update's download has got, between model.update_started and model.update_finished: about four a second at most, and one when every byte is on disk (done_bytes equal to total_bytes; model.update_finished then says whether the files checked out). A model already installed sends only that one.

id.description: The model being replaced (the same as next for a first download).

done_bytes.description: Bytes on disk so far across its files. It can go down: a file whose server ignores a resume starts over.

ModelUpdateFinished.description: A model update ended, and its hold is released.

id.description: The model that was to be replaced.

ok.description: Whether the new model is installed (and warm, if the old one was).

no_model_warm.description: The update left no model warm: dictation has no model until one is warmed.

message.description: Why it failed, when it did.

AudioDropped.description: The pump dropped capture blocks because a chain's queue was full (the chain fell behind). Sent once per stretch, when the queue takes audio again or closes.

channel.description: The side, for dictation (the mic). Absent for a meeting, whose two sides share one queue.

DictationVoiceDetection.description: Whether dictations are levelled with voice detection. Sent at the start and whenever it changes; while unavailable the shell shows it.

available.description: Whether a VAD is in use.

DictationStarted.description: A hold passed the minimum and is now a take: show that it is listening (or, with edit, that it is taking an instruction for the selection).

take.description: This take's number within the session: partials carry it, so a late one is never shown under the next take.

edit.description: A voice edit (the edit key) rather than a dictation.

mode.description: For a dictation: the mode it is expected to write in, by its name, from the app in front (the text is written in the mode of the app that receives it).

app.description: For a dictation: the name of the app in front, when the OS reported one.

DictationShortPressIgnored.description: A press shorter than the minimum hold (a modifier used in a shortcut). Nothing was shown or transcribed.

DictationStopped.description: The take is closed and being processed.

DictationDiscarded.description: The take ended without an insertion.

reason.description: Why. speech_too_short: tell the user it was too short and to try again.

live_ms.description: How long the key was held, for too_short.

DictationCommand.description: The take was a voice command.

value.description: Its argument: a style, a model id, a URL, an app path, or fixed text.

carried_out.description: Whether the core carried it out (change_style, toggle_polish and insert_text); the rest are recognised, so their words are not typed, but this build does not do them yet: say so. Absent from a core before 1.0.

DictationInserted.description: A dictation went out. Carries the user's words: never log it.

record.description: Its library record, unless saving failed.

DictationFailed.description: A take failed. Nothing was inserted for a transcription failure.

DictationWarningEvent.description: Something went wrong during a take, and it went on without it.

message.description: The error, where there was one.

DictationHotkeyLost.description: The OS removed the hotkey. Nothing more arrives until it is started again.

DictationWorkerFailed.description: A stage of the dictation chain panicked; the take in progress is lost. With recovered, the next take works. Without it the worker has stopped after repeated failures: the shell MUST unbind the dictation hotkey (unbind_hotkey is then true) and show that dictation is off, since key presses now reach nothing.

recovered.description: Whether the worker is still serving.

unbind_hotkey.description: The shell must unbind the hotkey now: always the opposite of recovered.

EditFailure.description: Why a voice edit left the selection alone. None of these changed the user's text. secure_input: Secure Input was on, so the selection was never read. not_allowed: the user has not agreed to send the selection where the model goes now (never agreed, or it changed destination since); nothing was sent, and message names the model.

DictationPartial.description: What the live engine hears while the key is held: settled words, then the current hypothesis. Each replaces the last; none is saved, and none arrives for a take after its dictation.stopped. Carries the user's words: never log it.

take.description: The take, as dictation.started numbered it.

DictationEdited.description: A voice edit replaced the selection with its rewrite. The rewrite is not saved to the library.

DictationEditFailed.description: A voice edit ended without touching the selection.

reason.description: Why. no_selection: ask the user to select text first. no_model: editing needs a language model.

message.description: The error, where there was one. Never the user's words.

DictationEditHotkeyLost.description: The OS removed the voice-edit key. Nothing more arrives from it until dictation is enabled again.

DictationReady.description: Dictation is live: the core holds the keys named here, and a hold of the key is a dictation. Sent in answer to dictation.enable, and again after a key setting changes.

key.description: The dictation key's token (for example fn or right_option).

edit_key.description: The voice-edit key's token, when one is set and bound.

edit_key_error.description: Why the voice-edit key set in the settings could not be bound; dictation works without it. Never the user's words.

settings_error.description: Which of dictation's settings could not be read (it runs with their defaults), as a sentence: "couldn't read the modes". Never the user's words.

ref.description: The command's "id", when it had one.

DictationOff.description: Dictation is not live: key presses reach nothing and no key is held. Sent in answer to dictation.enable and dictation.disable, and when dictation stops on its own (the worker stopped, Accessibility was revoked).

message.description: The error, where there was one. Never the user's words.

ref.description: The command's "id", when it had one.

DictationMicFailed.description: The microphone could not be opened for a take; the take was dropped. The next press tries again.

MeetingStarted.description: A meeting's record exists and its capture is being transcribed live. Names what the shell shows of it: its title, its app and its mic, when known. Sent for every meeting, however it started (Record, the consent Drop's offer, or an app's Always policy): the shell shows the recording indicator from this event, so a call recorded by its policy shows exactly as one the user started.

title.description: Its title, when known at the start (a calendar event, a replay's name); otherwise the summary's headline names it later.

app.description: The app it records, by id (a bundle id on the Mac), when it was started for one.

app_name.description: That app's name, as the shell shows it.

mic_name.description: The microphone it records, as the OS names it.

far_end.description: What it records as the other side.

auto.description: True when the app's call policy (Always) started it, without a tap: the shell says so where the recording shows, keeps the reminder to tell the others, and offers Stop and Stop and delete. Absent for a start the user made. A policy start always records the app's own sound alone (far_end app).

delete_until_unix_ms.description: Until this moment, Unix ms (a minute after the start), meeting.discard (Stop and delete) may delete this meeting as if it had never been made; after it only Stop is offered (meeting.discard is refused with delete_window_over). Absent for a meeting that cannot be deleted so (a replay).

MeetingFarEndFallback.description: The meeting was started for an app whose own sound could not be recorded alone, so it records everything this Mac plays instead (except Inkwell itself): other apps' sound is in the recording too. Sent once, right after meeting.started; the shell says so where the meeting shows.

app.description: The app it was started for, by id.

app_name.description: That app's name, as the shell shows it.

message.description: Why its sound could not be recorded alone (the platform's error). Never audio or words.

MeetingMicSwitched.description: A recording meeting's mic went (unplugged, switched off) and the meeting records with another now: the choice as it is now, else Automatic. A meeting never moves to a mic that was plugged in or made the default mid-call; only its own mic going moves it. The mic_* fields are meeting.started's, for the mic now.

from_name.description: The mic that went, as the OS named it, when known.

from_transport.description: How that mic connected, when known.

MeetingDetected.description: An app has held the microphone long enough to be a call, and no meeting is being recorded: the shell offers to record it (the consent Drop), and records only if the user says so (meeting.start with this app). Its policy is Ask (meetings.calls), or Always when its recording could not start by itself (message says why: a start that failed, or a far end that would not be the app's sound alone), when the user stopped a recording by hand during this call, or when the app was made Always during this call. The Drop can also set the app's policy (meetings.calls.set): Always (then meeting.start) or Never.

app.description: The app, by id (a bundle id on the Mac).

app_name.description: Its name, as the shell shows it.

message.description: Why it is offered rather than recorded, when its policy is Always: its recording could not start by itself (the platform's error), or its own sound cannot be recorded alone, so the recording would hold everything this computer plays (the Mac's fallback, Windows' device loopback): an Always app is recorded by itself only when its sound alone is. Never content.

MeetingDetectionEnded.description: The offer to record an app is over before it was taken: the app released the microphone, or the user said not this one (meeting.dismiss), or its policy became Never (meetings.calls.set).

dismissed.description: Whether the user dismissed it, by Not this one or Never (rather than the app releasing the microphone).

MeetingDetection.description: Whether the core is listening for calls now: sent once at start whatever the state (off included, with a message when the default call policy could not be read), then when detection starts, stops (the call policies: it listens while any app could be offered or recorded, so a default of Never with no app chosen for is off), fails to start, or stops on its own (the platform stopped answering). The shell shows this state, not the setting.

listening.description: Whether apps taking the microphone are being watched.

message.description: Why not, when detection could not start or stopped on its own. Never content.

CallPolicy.description: What happens when an app holds the microphone for a call: always (recorded at once, visibly, as by Record), ask (the consent Drop offers it) or never (neither).

CallApp.description: An app in the call policies' list: one detection has seen hold the microphone for a call, or one the user chose for. Never shown by its identity: a shell names it and shows its icon from the identity, as for a mode's apps.

app.description: Its identity, as detection reports it: a bundle id on the Mac, the executable (or the package's app id) on Windows, where it is kept in lowercase.

app_name.description: Its name as detection last saw it; absent for an app chosen for that has not been seen.

policy.description: What happens for it now: the user's choice, else the default (Always is Ask while the stored list could not be read).

chosen.description: Whether the user chose its policy; false while it follows the default.

seen_unix_ms.description: When detection last saw it hold the microphone for a call, Unix ms.

MeetingsCalls.description: The call policies: the default for apps not chosen for, and every app seen or chosen for (at most 64), most recently seen first. In answer to meetings.calls.list and meetings.calls.set (with ref), and unasked when the default changed or detection saw a new app.

default.description: The policy for apps not chosen for (meetings.calls.default; ask unless set).

message.description: Why the stored choices could not be read, while they are set aside: every app follows the default then, with Always lowered to Ask, and meetings.calls.set is refused (list_unreadable) unless it says replace_unreadable, which starts the list over. In the answer to that start over under a default of Always: that the default is Ask now (written), so the user sets Always again knowingly.

ref.description: The command's "id", when it had one, so the shell can match the answer to what it sent.

MeetingDiscarded.description: A meeting stopped with meeting.discard (Stop and delete), or one a crash interrupted on its way to being deleted, is gone as if it had never been made: no final pass ran and nothing was sent to a language model; its transcript, notes and search entries were deleted with their words overwritten in the library's files, then its audio. Follows meeting.stopped; no meeting.finished comes. The screens drop it.

audio_left.description: Its recorded audio is still on disk: it could not be removed, or its folder is outside the library and was left alone. The record itself is gone.

scrubbed.description: No copy of its words is left in the library's files (as for record.deleted).

MeetingAnswered.description: An answer to meeting.ask about the live meeting: the model's words. Render them as text only (no links): model text can say anything. A failure is command.failed with the command's id. Never log it.

ref.description: The id of the meeting.ask command this answers.

MeetingRecovered.description: A meeting a crash interrupted is being finished: its recorded audio was repaired and its final pass follows (its events, ending in meeting.finished or meeting.failed).

trimmed.description: Torn partial frames cut from a chunk's end.

unrecoverable.description: Chunk files left as they were: nothing could place them.

recorded_ms.description: How much audio the meeting recorded before the crash, ms.

meetings.description: Interrupted meetings it finished or tried to.

message.description: Present when the meetings could not even be looked for (the data directory could not be listed): an interrupted meeting may be waiting, and the next launch looks again. Names what failed, never a meeting's words.

MicTransport.description: How a device connects: built in, Bluetooth (call-quality audio, and zeros while its user is silent), USB, a virtual or aggregate device, or anything else.

MicReason.description: Why Inkwell records this microphone: the one the user chose in Settings > Sound (chosen, found by its id or by its name and transport); Automatic standing in for a chosen mic that is not connected (chosen_missing); or Automatic's reason: the system default input; the built-in mic because the output is Bluetooth (a headset mic is call-quality audio; on Windows a USB mic may be the one kept); the headset's own mic because a platform's retired headset-mic switch is on; the default because this Mac has no built-in mic (on Windows: every mic is Bluetooth); the first input because no default is set; it was named; the LE Audio headset's own mic, which keeps full quality (Windows); or a reason this build of the core does not name (unknown).

FarEnd.description: What a meeting records as the other side: the sound of its app alone (a call recorded from the consent Drop's offer), or everything this Mac plays except Inkwell itself (Record now, which names no app, or a call whose app could not be heard alone: meeting.far_end_fallback says so).

MeetingVoiceDetection.description: Whether a side is levelled with voice detection. Sent per side at the start and when it changes.

available.description: Whether a VAD is in use.

MeetingSideState.description: What a side is delivering, when that changes.

MeetingPartial.description: Provisional live text; each replaces the last and none is saved. Carries the meeting's words: never log it.

MeetingFinal.description: Settled live text, saved as revision 1. Carries the meeting's words: never log it.

MeetingWarningEvent.description: Something went wrong in a meeting, and it went on without it. Which fields are present depends on kind.

start_ms.description: Start of the stretch, ms into the meeting.

quiet_ms.description: How long the far end was without signal, ms.

audible_ms.description: Time above the audible floor, ms; for echo_path_not_found, while the far end played.

chunks.description: Chunk files skipped or cut short.

message.description: The error, where there was one. Never the meeting's words.

MeetingStopped.description: Capture ended and the record is marked ended; the final pass runs next.

MeetingTranscribed.description: The final pass finished one side.

MeetingDiarized.description: Diarization of the far end finished.

substantial.description: Clusters holding at least 2 % of the far end's speech.

labelled.description: Whether the labels were kept: at least two substantial clusters.

EchoState.description: Whether the live mic is protected from the far end's echo. searching: no echo path yet, the mic reaches the live transcript as captured (unprotected; with earbuds there is none to find); cancelling: a path was found, the live you transcript hears the cancelled mic behind the echo gate; degraded: cancelling, but the linear stage takes almost no echo off; failed: cancellation stopped, and the search starts again; found_at_end: at the end, the search that was still running found a path, so the mic went unprotected throughout it.

EchoSearch.description: Why the live echo search (re)started: the meeting started, the capture's device changed (a new device is a new echo path), or cancellation failed.

EchoFailure.description: Why echo cancellation stopped: backlog (one side ran more than 10 s ahead of the other; channel says which), bad_alignment (a path no canceller follows), stalled (the canceller gave no answer in time; it is left behind), internal (a bug inside the core, reported rather than hidden).

MeetingEcho.description: Whether the live mic is protected from echo, when it changes. Which fields are present depends on state.

why.description: Why the search began, for searching.

since_ms.description: Where the search began, ms into the meeting, for searching.

from_ms.description: Where cancellation began, ms into the meeting, for cancelling.

unprotected_ms.description: How long the mic went uncancelled since the search began, ms, for cancelling (0 when cancellation carries on along a better fit) and found_at_end.

stable_from_ms.description: Where the search's windows first supported the path, ms into the meeting, for cancelling and found_at_end.

delay_ms.description: How late the mic hears the far end, ms, for cancelling.

drift_ppm.description: How fast the mic's clock runs against the far end's, ppm, for cancelling.

erle_db.description: The linear stage's echo return loss enhancement over the last 20 s of far-end audio, dB, for degraded.

channel.description: The side that ran ahead, for a backlog.

EchoPath.description: The echo path the final pass fitted over the whole recording.

delay_ms.description: How late the mic hears the far end at the start, ms.

drift_ppm.description: How fast the mic's clock runs against the far end's, ppm.

stable_from_ms.description: Where the windows first supported it, ms into the meeting.

MeetingEchoPass.description: What echo cancellation did in the final pass. Sent before the supersede.

path.description: The path, when the recording has one.

candidates.description: Windows loud and clear enough to vote.

cancelled.description: Whether the mic was cancelled (false: no path, or cancellation failed).

erle_first_db.description: Echo return loss enhancement over the first 10 s of far-end audio, dB.

erle_db.description: Echo return loss enhancement over far-end audio after that, dB.

linear_erle_db.description: The same for the linear output alone (what the you transcript hears), dB.

removed.description: You lines removed as echo of the far end.

kept_near_speech.description: Lines that repeated the far end but were kept: the near end was heard over them.

kept_no_evidence.description: Lines that repeated the far end but were kept for want of acoustic evidence.

live_echo_finals.description: Live you finals the pass judged to be echo; the supersede guard does not count them.

start_ms.description: Its start, ms into the meeting.

RemovedEchoLine.description: A you line the final pass removed as echo of the far end. Its words are not here: the store keeps the line with the record, at index in its removed lines (by start time), so it can be put back.

index.description: Its place in the record's removed lines.

start_ms.description: Its start, ms into the meeting.

far.description: The far-end lines whose words it matched, in time order.

matched.description: How many of them matched the far end, in order.

MeetingRemovedAsEcho.description: You lines the final pass removed as echo, by place and span only. Sent only when there are some, before the supersede.

MeetingSuperseded.description: The final pass replaced the live transcript.

MeetingKeptLive.description: The final pass did not replace the live transcript, which stays as it was.

unverified.description: Items dropped because their citation did not check out.

MeetingLooksDone.description: In this meeting the user said work was already done that earlier meetings' open commitments promise: each such commitment now carries a "looks done" suggestion (commitments.list shows it) for the user to confirm or dismiss. Sent only when there is at least one.

MeetingFinished.description: Everything is done: the record is complete.

revision.description: The transcript's revision now; absent only when the live one was kept and the record could not be read.

MeetingFailed.description: A meeting could not start, or its final pass stopped before replacing the live transcript (which then stands, and the pass can run again).

record.description: The meeting's record, when it had one.

MeetingCaptureFailed.description: Capture stopped because the core's pump failed (a bug in the core, contained). What reached disk is kept: the meeting ends as if capture had stopped, and its final pass runs over it.

record.description: The meeting's record, when it had one.

MeetingWorkerFailed.description: The meeting's worker panicked and stopped. Its recorded audio is on disk; the live transcript so far is saved.

PermissionState.description: A permission's state, as the platform's probe reads it without prompting.

PermissionName.description: A permission the app depends on.

ModeStyle.description: How a mode writes: a style this build knows, or other.

OwedItem.description: An open commitment: not done, and not merged into another.

record.description: The record it was said in.

record_title.description: That record's title, when it has one.

record_started_at_unix_ms.description: When that record started, Unix ms.

recipient.description: Who it is owed to, as said, when the transcript says.

due_at_unix_ms.description: When, resolved to a time, Unix ms: what overdue is measured against.

said_at_ms.description: Where in the record it was first said, ms.

merged.description: How many other commitments were merged into it as the same promise said again.

looks_done.description: Where a later meeting suggests it is already done, until the user answers.

DoneEvidence.description: Where a later meeting suggests an open commitment is already done: the user said, there, that they had finished it. A suggestion for the user to confirm (commitment.set_done) or dismiss (commitment.not_yet).

record.description: The record it was said in.

record_title.description: That record's title, when it has one.

record_started_at_unix_ms.description: When that record started, Unix ms.

text.description: The line said there, when it is still in the record's transcript. The library's words: never log it.

ModeInfo.description: A mode: how dictation writes in the apps it names. Carries the user's words (its name, polish instructions and apps): never log it.

name.description: Its name, as the user sees and says it.

polish.description: Whether its dictations are polished (when a language model can).

polish_prompt.description: Its polish instructions, as the user wrote them; blank for the default (modes.listed's default_polish_prompt). The user's words: never log them.

polish_model.description: The language model it is polished on, by its id in polish_models; absent for the AI setting's (setting_polish_model). Whether a take can use it now is polish_model_state.

remove_fillers.description: Whether fillers and stutters are removed.

apps.description: The apps it is picked for, matched against the frontmost app's identity. Never shown to the user as they are: a shell names each app.

items.description: An app identity, or part of one: on macOS a bundle id such as com.example.mail.

polish_model_name.description: A model at the provider polish_model names (provider: ids only), sent as the request's model on the same endpoint; absent for the model chosen with the provider in Settings > AI. Free text the user typed: never log it.

polish_model_state.description: With polish_model: whether its takes can use it now.

LanguageModelChoice.description: A language model a mode can be polished on: one the shell registered, or the own-key provider chosen in Settings > AI.

id.description: Its id, as a mode names it (polish_model): engine:<id> for a model the shell registered (engine:apple-foundation-models), provider:<id> for the chosen own-key provider. Show the name, never the id.

name.description: Its name, as consent.state names a model (a shell may name its own engine better).

endpoint.description: For a cloud model, the endpoint it sends to, as consent.state names one. To confirm a mode's model (polish_model_state moved or unrecorded), show where it sends and send that back as polish_model_confirm_to: {"to":"on_device"} or {"to":"cloud","endpoint":"<this>"}.

allowed.description: Whether polish may use it now: one of the user's polish consents covers it (consent.state's consents) and local-only mode lets it (blocked_local_only false). False, a mode on it goes in as said (polish_not_allowed, or polish_failed while local-only mode refuses it) until that changes.

model.description: The model it asks for: for the own-key provider, the one chosen in Settings > AI, which a mode's polish_model_name replaces (the editor's placeholder).

blocked_local_only.description: Local-only mode is on and this model is not on this machine: nothing goes to it, whatever the consent (turn local-only off in Settings > AI first).

PermissionsChecked.description: Every permission's state now, in answer to permissions.check. Never prompts. System audio reads not_determined until the app has asked for it, because checking it before would make macOS prompt.

system_audio.description: Recording other apps' sound (the far end), verified by listening for the app's own tone.

accessibility.description: Typing into other apps, reading the focused app and the dictation key. Never asked reads as denied.

input_monitoring.description: A listen-only key tap, which the Mac app does not use. Never asked reads as denied.

PermissionRequested.description: permission.request showed the system prompt or opened the settings pane. The answer comes later: check again when the user comes back.

CommitmentsListed.description: The open commitments across the library, in answer to commitments.list: the soonest resolved due time first, undated ones last. Carries the promises' words.

CommitmentUpdated.description: A commitment was marked done or open again (commitment.set_done), or its looks-done suggestion was dismissed (commitment.not_yet). Either way, a suggestion on it is settled.

NoteAdded.description: A note was saved to a record, in answer to note.add. Its words stay with the shell that sent them.

at_ms.description: Where in the record it was written, ms.

ref.description: The command's "id", when it had one, so the shell can match the note to what it sent.
The command's "id", when it had one, so the shell can match the answer to the line that sent it.
The command's "id", when it had one, so the shell can match the answer to the line that sent it.

SpeakerNamed.description: A far-end speaker of a record was named, renamed or cleared, in answer to speaker.name. The name stays with the shell that sent it: record.open carries it.

named.description: Whether the speaker has a name now: false when it was cleared, and reads as numbered again.

ref.description: The command's "id", when it had one, so the shell can match the answer to what it sent.

RecordDeleted.description: A record was deleted whole, in answer to record.delete: its transcript, notes, summary, commitments, speaker names and search entries, its words overwritten in the library's files as the retention setting deletes them, then its audio. The screens drop it.

audio_left.description: Its recorded audio is still on disk: it could not be removed, or its folder is outside the library and was left alone. The record itself is gone.

scrubbed.description: No copy of its words is left in the library's files. False, as for deleted_text_not_scrubbed, while another process reading the database keeps them in its log: the deletion is saved, and the library keeps trying; a dictation's or meeting's deleted_text_scrubbed says when it has. This answer counts as that change's report: each change reaches the shell once.

ref.description: The command's "id", when it had one, so the shell can match the answer to what it sent.

ModelsListed.description: The catalogue's models for this OS, in answer to models.list and model.remove. What serves each job now is engine.route's answer.

models.description: The models, in the catalogue's order.

free_bytes.description: The bytes free to this user on the volume models are installed on; absent when the OS could not say.

ref.description: The command's "id", when it had one.

SettingValue.description: A shell setting's value, in answer to setting.get or setting.set.

value.description: Its value; absent when it has never been set.

AudioDevices.description: The answer to audio.devices: the devices, the user's choice, and what Inkwell records with now.

inputs.description: The connected microphones, the default first.

input.description: The mic choice (audio.input): auto, or the chosen device's id.

wanted.description: The chosen mic as remembered, when input is a device: Settings shows its name even while it is not connected.

automatic.description: What Automatic records now ("Automatic (<name>)"); absent when there is no microphone.

using.description: The mic Inkwell opens now for a take, a meeting or a test, and why: the chosen one, or Automatic (chosen_missing when it stands in for a chosen mic that is not connected). Absent when there is no microphone. A meeting already recording keeps its own mic (meeting.started, meeting.mic_switched).

outputs.description: The connected outputs, the default first, where there is an output picker (Windows); absent on macOS, whose far end is tapped from its app wherever it plays.

output.description: The output choice (audio.output), with outputs: default, or the chosen device's id.

output_wanted.description: The chosen output as remembered, when output is a device.

output_using.description: The output a meeting's far end is to record, and why; absent when there is no output. Stored and shown now; meetings record it once the Windows far end is pinned to it, and until then follow the default output.

ref.description: The id of the command this answers, when it carried one.

AudioDevicesChanged.description: Devices came or went, a default changed, or the choice did: the same as audio.devices, once a burst of changes has gone quiet (300 ms after the last, at most 1 s after the first). Sent after a setting.set of audio.input or audio.output, and on a device change where the platform tells the core of them.

inputs.description: The connected microphones, the default first.

input.description: The mic choice (audio.input): auto, or the chosen device's id.

wanted.description: The chosen mic as remembered, when input is a device: Settings shows its name even while it is not connected.

automatic.description: What Automatic records now ("Automatic (<name>)"); absent when there is no microphone.

using.description: The mic Inkwell opens now for a take, a meeting or a test, and why: the chosen one, or Automatic (chosen_missing when it stands in for a chosen mic that is not connected). Absent when there is no microphone. A meeting already recording keeps its own mic (meeting.started, meeting.mic_switched).

outputs.description: The connected outputs, the default first, where there is an output picker (Windows); absent on macOS, whose far end is tapped from its app wherever it plays.

output.description: The output choice (audio.output), with outputs: default, or the chosen device's id.

output_wanted.description: The chosen output as remembered, when output is a device.

output_using.description: The output a meeting's far end is to record, and why; absent when there is no output. Stored and shown now; meetings record it once the Windows far end is pinned to it, and until then follow the default output.

AudioInputFallback.description: The mic the user chose is not connected, and a mic just opened on Automatic in its place (a take, a meeting, a meeting's mic that went, a test): said once until the chosen mic is seen again or the choice changes. The shell says "<wanted> isn't connected. Inkwell is using <mic> until it is."

mic_name.description: The mic recording instead, as the OS names it.

AudioTestStarted.description: A mic test has opened the mic (audio.test): the one dictation and meetings would use now. audio.test_level follows about ten times a second, then audio.tested.

mic_name.description: The mic, as the OS names it.

seconds.description: How long the test runs at most, in seconds.

ref.description: The id of the command this answers, when it carried one.

AudioTestLevel.description: The mic test's level over the last 100 ms: the loudest moment, from the ink's band analyzer with no gain applied, on a meter scale.

level.description: 0 at -60 dBFS and below, 1 at full scale, linear in dB between.

ref.description: The id of the command this answers, when it carried one.

AudioTested.description: The mic test is over. Nothing it heard was kept.

heard.description: Whether the mic heard anything louder than a quiet room (-50 dBFS) at any moment: false is the screen's cue for "Not hearing you?".

peak.description: The loudest moment, on audio.test_level's scale.

message.description: Why it failed, naming the device, when ended is failed.

ref.description: The id of the command this answers, when it carried one.

AudioDevice.description: A connected input or output device.

id.description: The OS's id for it (a Core Audio UID, a WASAPI endpoint id): what audio.input and audio.output take. Opaque: never shown.

name.description: Its name as the OS shows it.

is_default.description: Whether it is the system default for its direction.

AudioWanted.description: A device the user chose, as the core remembers it from when it was chosen (it may not be connected now).

name.description: Its name when it was chosen; absent for a choice stored without one.

transport.description: How it connected when it was chosen; absent likewise.

AudioInput.description: A microphone Inkwell picks, and why.

name.description: Its name as the OS shows it.

AudioOutput.description: The output a meeting's far end is to record (Windows), and why. Stored and shown now; meetings record it once the Windows far end is pinned to it, and until then follow the default output.

name.description: Its name as the OS shows it.

OutputReason.description: Why a meeting's far end records this output (Windows): the one the user chose (chosen), the default because the chosen one is not connected (chosen_missing), or the default output, chosen (default_output).

AudioTestEnd.description: How a mic test ended: its time was up (done), audio.test_stop or the core's shutdown ended it (stopped), a meeting started recording (meeting), or the mic failed or went away (failed, with a message).

HotkeyChecked.description: Whether this computer can watch a key binding as the dictation key or the edit key, in answer to hotkey.check. A shell checks a shortcut the user recorded before it stores it with setting.set; nothing is stored here.

binding.description: The binding as the command spelled it.

ok.description: Whether this computer can watch it.

canonical.description: When ok: its one spelling, to store with setting.set and to compare keys by (two spellings of one chord are one key). For example ctrl+shift+space, right_option or f13.

reason.description: When not ok: why not, in plain words starting in lower case and without a full stop, to show after "can't use that:". For example "that key on its own would stop working everywhere else; add Control, Option or Command".

ref.description: The command's "id", when it had one.

LlmFeature.description: A feature that sends the user's words to a language model, each with its own consent: polish (the dictation, before it is typed), edit (voice edit: the selection and the spoken instruction) or meetings (a meeting's summary, its commitments and Ask: the meeting's transcript).

LlmDestination.description: Where a feature sends the user's words: on_device (a model on this machine; the words stay on it) or cloud (a model elsewhere; the words leave this machine for its provider).

ConsentState.description: A feature that sends the user's words to a language model: its switch, where the model it would use now sends them, and where the user agreed it may. The feature runs only when on and allowed. In answer to consent.get, consent.allow and consent.revoke, and after the feature's switch is set to off.

on.description: Its switch: dictation.polish on, a voice-edit key set, or meetings.llm on.

to.description: Where the model it would use now sends; absent when no language model is registered.

name.description: That model's name, as the shell registered it (a cloud provider's name); absent with to.

endpoint.description: For cloud, the destination consent.allow must name; absent otherwise.

allowed_to.description: Where the user agreed it may send: for polish, the consent covering the model it would use now, else the first (all of them are consents); absent when never agreed (or turned off since).

allowed_name.description: For a cloud consent, the provider's name the user agreed to.

allowed.description: Whether a consent covers the model it would use now: false while the feature is on means it is paused until the user agrees again. For polish, a mode on its own model is judged on that model (modes.listed's polish_models).

consents.description: Every destination the user agreed the feature may send to. Polish holds one per destination (a mode may polish on a model elsewhere than the AI setting's: consent.allow adds one, consent.revoke takes one away); voice edit and meetings hold one at most.

error.description: Why part of this could not be read (the switch or the consent), as a sentence starting "couldn't". An unread switch counts as off, an unread consent as none.

ref.description: The command's "id", when it had one.

LlmProviderEntry.description: An own-key (BYOK) language model provider the user can choose: its id, what it uses unless told otherwise, and whether its API key is stored. The key itself never leaves the OS key store.

id.description: The provider: openai, groq, anthropic, openrouter or custom (any OpenAI-compatible server).

default_model.description: The model used when llm.choose names none.

endpoint.description: Its address: fixed for a built-in provider; for custom, the address used when llm.choose names none.

custom_url.description: Whether llm.choose may name another address (custom only).

needs_key.description: Whether a call needs its API key (a custom server usually runs without one).

has_key.description: Whether a key is stored for it in the OS key store, asked without reading the key. False when that could not be asked (llm.providers' error says so).

LlmProviders.description: The own-key language model providers and the one chosen, in answer to llm.providers, llm.key.save, llm.key.delete and llm.choose. A feature (polish, voice edit, summaries and Ask) sends to the chosen provider only when no model is registered by the shell, and only with the user's consent for its endpoint (consent.state).

chosen.description: The chosen provider's id; absent when none is chosen.

model.description: The model the chosen provider is asked for; absent with chosen.

base_url.description: For custom, the server's address as chosen; absent otherwise.

endpoint.description: Where the chosen provider sends, as consent.state names it; absent with chosen.

to.description: Whether the chosen provider is on this machine (on_device) or not (cloud); absent with chosen.

local_only.description: Local-only mode (llm.local_only): while on, a provider that is not on this machine is never called.

ready.description: Whether the chosen provider can be called: its key is stored (when it needs one), and local-only mode lets it through. Each feature still needs its own consent.

error.description: What could not be read (the stored keys, or the choice), as a sentence starting "couldn't"; absent when all was read.

ref.description: The command's "id", when it had one.

LlmTested.description: The answer to llm.test: one short fixed request (never the user's words) sent to the chosen provider with its stored key, and whether it answered.

status.description: The HTTP status of a refusal (401 or 403: the key; 404: the model or address; 429: the account's limits); absent otherwise.

error.description: Why it did not answer, as a sentence starting "couldn't"; absent when ok. Names what failed, never the key.

ref.description: The command's "id", when it had one.

ModesListed.description: The user's modes, in answer to modes.list, modes.save and modes.delete, in the order they are matched: the first mode naming the frontmost app wins, else the default. Carries the user's words: never log it.

default_id.description: The mode used when no other matches.

default_polish_prompt.description: The polish instructions a mode with blank ones uses: the editor's placeholder.

polish_models.description: Every language model a mode can be polished on now, the AI setting's first. Empty when the core holds none.

setting_polish_model.description: The id (in polish_models) of the model a mode without one of its own is polished on now: the AI setting's. Absent when there is none.

saved.description: In answer to modes.save: the id of the mode saved (a new mode's id is the core's), so the editor can select it.

ref.description: The command's "id", when it had one.

SnippetsListed.description: The user's snippets, in answer to snippets.list or snippets.save. Carries the user's words: never log it.

snippets.description: The snippets, in the user's order.

from_import.description: They are the ones the Inkwell 0.2 import brought, not yet saved in 1.0.

ref.description: The command's id.

SnippetInfo.description: A snippet: a spoken trigger that dictation replaces with its expansion.

trigger.description: What the user says, matched as whole words in any case.

expansion.description: What it becomes; {date}, {time} and {clipboard} are filled in.

VoiceCommandsListed.description: The voice commands, in answer to voice_commands.list or voice_commands.save. Carries the user's words: never log it.

enabled.description: Whether any dictation can be a command.

wake_prefix.description: The word a command starts with.

commands.description: The commands, in order of precedence.

from_import.description: They are the ones the Inkwell 0.2 import brought, not yet saved in 1.0.

ref.description: The command's id.

VoiceCommandInfo.description: A voice command and the phrases that trigger it.

triggers.description: The phrases, any of which triggers it after the wake word.

value.description: Its argument: a style, a model id, a URL, an app path, or fixed text.

carried_out.description: Whether this build carries the action out.

ImportNotes.description: What the Inkwell 0.2 import has to tell the user once, in answer to import.notes.

key.description: What became of 0.2's dictation hotkey; absent when there is nothing to say or the user dismissed it.

ref.description: The command's id.

ImportKeyNote.description: 0.2's dictation hotkey, and what the import made of it.

hotkey.description: 0.2's hotkey as it stored it: a modifier token (fn, right_cmd, ...) or a combination such as super+shift+space.

key.description: The 1.0 dictation key it became, when it did.

applied.description: The import set it as the dictation key (a key already chosen in 1.0 is kept).

toggle.description: 0.2 started and stopped on separate presses; 1.0 is hold to talk.

ImportKeyOutcome.description: What became of 0.2's dictation hotkey: mapped to a 1.0 key (the same key), replaced by another key because this OS never sees it (Fn on Windows becomes right Ctrl; key names both), or not carried over, because it is a combination or another key 1.0 cannot hold on its own.

ImportChecked.description: What import.check found: Inkwell 0.2's data at 0.2's own data directory on this computer (the core knows where), and whether this library holds it already. The data is read, never written, and the keychain is not asked, so linked_keys is 0 here.

state.description: Whether there is something to import.

counts.description: What an import would bring (the dry run), when found.

message.description: Why the data cannot be read now, when unreadable: words to show (for one, that Inkwell 0.2 is still open and should be quit first).

ref.description: The command's id.

ImportState.description: Inkwell 0.2's data: found (and not imported yet), absent from this computer, imported into this library already (0.2's data is not opened then), or found but unreadable now (import.run may still work once the reason is gone).

ImportCounts.description: How many of each kind Inkwell 0.2's data holds, or an import wrote.

dictations.description: Dictations, each a record in the library.

dictionary_entries.description: Dictionary entries (a word and what replaces it).

linked_keys.description: Providers whose API key in the keychain is linked, by reference (never copied).

ImportFinished.description: import.run brought Inkwell 0.2's data into the library, in one transaction: the library's records changed (list them again), import.notes may have something to say about the dictation key, and a running dictation already uses what came over. A failure is command.failed, its message in words to show.

ref.description: The command's id.

ModelKind.description: What a model in the catalogue is for: speech (transcription, live words, voice detection, the diarizer) or language (polish, voice edit, a meeting's summary and Ask, run by the core on this computer; Windows only).

CatalogueEntry.description: A model in the catalogue that runs on this OS.

kind.description: What it is for. Always sent; a shell built before language models reads its absence as speech.

name.description: For a language model, its name for the user (Qwen3 4B Instruct); absent for a speech model, which the shell names itself.

suggested.description: For a language model, whether it is the size the core suggests for this computer: the Default, or the Small one with under 12 GB of memory (12 × 10⁹ bytes as the OS reports it). Exactly one language model is suggested where there are any; absent for a speech model.

installed.description: Whether its files are installed and complete.

jobs.description: The jobs it fills, each with its measured error rate. None for a model the core only downloads because the shell runs it (the Mac's Parakeet, parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-coreml), and none for a language model.

items.description: A job and its error rate.

RecordKind.description: What produced a record: one dictation, a meeting (mic and far end), or an imported audio or video file.

AudioTimeline.description: How a record's chunks were placed on its timeline: recorded (from the start the meeting wrote beside them) or estimated (from its earliest chunk, because that start is missing: an older record, or one whose write failed). Estimated: the two sides may be out of step, and the shell says so.

RecordRow.description: A record as a list shows it.

title.description: Its title: a calendar event's, a file's name, or the summary's headline. Absent until one is known.

ended_at_unix_ms.description: When it ended, Unix ms; absent while it is live.

revision.description: The transcript revision: 1 while live, 2 once the final pass replaced it.

has_audio.description: Whether it kept audio (a meeting's chunks).

preview.description: The first words of an untitled record's transcript. Carries the user's words: never log it.

RecordSegment.description: Settled transcript on a record's timeline. Carries the user's words: never log it.

start_ms.description: Start, ms from the record's start.

end_ms.description: End, ms from the record's start.

speaker.description: The diarized far-end speaker, when labels were kept.

RecordNote.description: A note the user typed, stamped with where in the record it was written.

at_ms.description: Where in the record, ms from its start: the timestamp chip.

text.description: The note. The user's words: never log it.

RecordSummary.description: A record's summary, as stored: markdown (a headline, then sections). Shells render it; it is never shown raw.

text.description: The markdown. The library's words: never log it.

created_at_unix_ms.description: When it was written, Unix ms.

items.description: Its decisions and actions with the line each cites, in the order the text lists them (empty for a summary saved before they were kept).

SummaryItemKind.description: Whether a summary item is a decision or an action.

SummaryItemRow.description: A decision or an action in a summary, with the line it cites.

text.description: The item as the summary states it. The library's words: never log it.

span.description: Where the line it cites was said.

Span.description: A stretch of a record: where something was said.

start_ms.description: Start, ms from the record's start.

end_ms.description: End, ms from the record's start.

CommitmentRow.description: A commitment: something promised in a record.

text.description: What was promised. The library's words: never log it.

recipient.description: Who it is owed to, as said, when the transcript says.

due_at_unix_ms.description: When, resolved, Unix ms; absent when it could not be resolved.

provenance.description: Where in the record it was said.

merged_into.description: The commitment it was folded into ("said twice"), when it was.

looks_done.description: Where a later meeting suggests it is already done, until the user answers.

SpeakerName.description: A diarized speaker the user named in one record.

AudioChunk.description: One chunk file of a record's audio: raw little-endian float samples, interleaved, after a header of data_offset bytes.

start_ms.description: Where its first frame falls on the record's timeline, ms (negative: before the start).

RecordAudio.description: Where a record's audio is: its chunks per side, placed on its timeline.

chunks.description: Readable chunks, mic first then far end, each in order. Unreadable ones are left out (and logged).

left_out.description: Chunk files left out of the player: unreadable, or whose format or place on the timeline recovery could only guess. Nonzero: some of the audio cannot be played or placed, and the shell says so.

title.description: The record's title, when it has one.

started_at_unix_ms.description: When the record started, Unix ms.

start_ms.description: Where in the record the match is, ms.

snippet.description: The matching text. The library's words: never log it.

KindStats.description: What the library holds of one kind since a moment.

duration_ms.description: Their total length, ms (records still live count nothing).

LibraryRecords.description: Records, in answer to records.list: newest first (by start time, then id).

ref.description: The id of the command this answers, echoed so the shell can match the answer to its question.

kind.description: The kind asked for; absent for every kind.

more.description: Whether more records follow the last one: ask again with it as "before".

LibrarySearch.description: Full-text matches, in answer to records.search, best first.

ref.description: The id of the command this answers, echoed so the shell can match the answer to its question.

query.description: The query, as asked. The user's words: never log it.

LibraryRecord.description: One record whole, in answer to record.open. Carries the library's words: never log it.

ref.description: The id of the command this answers, echoed so the shell can match the answer to its question.

segments.description: The current revision's transcript, by start time.

summary.description: Its summary, when one was written.

commitments.description: Its commitments, in the order they were added, merged ones included.

audio.description: Its audio, when it kept some and the directory is there.

LibraryStats.description: What the library holds since a moment, in answer to library.stats, and whether recent meetings kept no far end.

ref.description: The id of the command this answers, echoed so the shell can match the answer to its question.

since_unix_ms.description: The moment asked about, Unix ms.

far_silent_meetings.description: The newest finished meetings in a row (of the last 20) that kept the user's words and none of the far end's: the sign that the other side was not heard.

far_silent_since_unix_ms.description: When the earliest of those started, Unix ms.

LibrarySwept.description: The retention setting deleted meetings and dictations older than it keeps (never imports), at launch, after a meeting, or when it changed. Their text is overwritten in the library's files, their audio removed.

failed.description: Records, or their audio, that could not be removed (each logged by what failed).

before_unix_ms.description: Records that started before this moment were due, Unix ms.

DictationStats.description: The user's dictation, counted on this computer: finished dictations by the local day they started. Speed and time saved count only dictations that know how long the key was held.

words_week.description: Words dictated since this week started (the shell's first weekday).

wpm_week.description: Words per minute this week: words over the time the key was held. Absent with less than a minute of speech this week.

wpm_average.description: Words per minute over the last 30 days, today included: the user's own average. Absent with less than a minute of speech in them.

saved_ms_week.description: Time saved this week, ms: the same words typed at typing_wpm less the time spent speaking. Negative when speaking took longer.

saved_ms_all.description: Time saved all time, ms, as saved_ms_week.

saved_about_week.description: What saved_ms_week is about, largest first ("about two feature films"). Absent when there is nothing to picture: time lost, under about 12 minutes, or between two counts.

saved_about_all.description: What saved_ms_all is about, as saved_about_week.

streak_days.description: The current streak: local days with a dictation in a row, one missed day forgiven, two ending it. A rest day neither counts nor breaks it, with a dictation or without; a paused day without a dictation is not missed, and one with a dictation counts. Running while at most one day was missed since the last active one (today is never missed).

latest_streak_days.description: The latest streak, running or ended: what it reached. Once a streak has ended, the shell shows this and the longest, never a streak as lost.

active_days_month.description: Local days with a dictation since the month started.

streak_hidden.description: Whether the user hid the streak (stats.streak): show no streak line and offer none on the share card. The numbers are still counted.

rest_days.description: The weekdays the streak rests on (stats.rest_days), ISO: 1 Monday to 7 Sunday; empty for none. A rest day neither counts nor breaks the streak.

streak_paused_since.description: The first day of the pause running today (streak.pause), YYYY-MM-DD. Absent while none runs; a pause ends by itself after 90 days.

heatmap_first_day.description: The heatmap's first local day, YYYY-MM-DD: the first day of the week eleven weeks before this one.

heatmap_words.description: Words dictated per local day, from heatmap_first_day to today.

MeetingStats.description: Meetings recorded here and finished, counted (imported meetings are left out: their channels came from elsewhere). Me versus them is stream identity: the mic is the user, the far end everyone else.

you_ms.description: The user's talk time, ms: how long their lines cover.

longest_monologue_ms.description: The user's longest stretch of speech with no one else speaking and no pause over 3 seconds, ms.

questions.description: The user's lines ending in a question mark: a plain count.

PromiseStats.description: Promises from meetings (commitments not merged into another), in Owed's states.

made.description: Promises made: kept, open and overdue together.

open.description: Not done, and not past their due day.

overdue.description: Not done, past their due day (due today is not late).

MilestoneKind.description: What a milestone counts: words dictated all time, or the longest streak in days.

MilestoneName.description: A milestone's name, a key the shells word: first_page (1,000 words), notebook (10,000), short_novel (50,000), novels_worth (100,000), seven_days, thirty_days and hundred_days (streaks).

MilestoneRow.description: A milestone and whether the library has reached it.

id.description: Its id: words_1000, words_10000, words_50000, words_100000, streak_7, streak_30, streak_100.

name.description: Its name, worded by the shell: the same on the chip, in the celebration and on the share card's seal.

TimeEquivalentKey.description: Something time saved is about, as long as: working_week 40 h, working_day 8 h, feature_film 2 h, lunch_hour 1 h, coffee_break 15 min.

TimeEquivalent.description: Time saved, pictured: about count of key, the nearest whole number, within a fifth of the time. Always said with "about".

count.description: How many: 1 to 5, or any number of the largest (working_week).

BestId.description: A personal best: the dictation held longest, the fastest held at least 30 s (neither a take the stuck-key watchdog stopped), the most words in a day, the best week, the longest meeting, the longest monologue.

BestUnit.description: What a best's value counts: ms, words a minute, or words.

date.description: When, YYYY-MM-DD: the take's local day, the day, or the week's first day.

record.description: The take holding it, for a take's best; absent for a day's or a week's.

BestNews.description: A best just set, for a short note in the Drop (a dictation's) or at the meeting's end (a meeting's).

record.description: The take holding it, as a BestRow's record.

WeekReview.description: Last week, reviewed: gains and plain facts only, nothing said to be down.

week.description: Its first day, YYYY-MM-DD: what stats.review_dismissed takes to dismiss it (kept dismissed if the week's first day changes later).

saved_ms.description: Time saved, ms, as saved_ms_week. Absent unless there was some.

saved_about.description: What saved_ms is about, as saved_about_week.

best_day.description: The day with the most words, YYYY-MM-DD (the earliest on a tie). Absent without words.

wpm.description: Words per minute, with at least a minute of speech.

wpm_gain.description: How many words a minute faster than the four weeks before it. Absent unless it was faster: a slower week is never compared.

promises_kept.description: Of the promises made in its meetings, those done now (no time is kept for when one was done). Absent when none.

StatsCounted.description: The Stats screen's numbers, in answer to stats.get, streak.pause or streak.resume: counted on this computer from the library, on the user's calendar. Nothing here is sent anywhere or drawn from what was said.

ref.description: The id of the command this answers, echoed so the shell can match the answer to its question.

today.description: Today on the user's calendar, YYYY-MM-DD.

typing_wpm.description: The typing speed time saved is measured against (stats.typing_wpm, 40 unless set).

promises_month.description: Promises made in meetings that started this month.

milestones.description: Every milestone, in a fixed order; with the streak hidden, the words milestones only.

bests.description: The user's personal bests, from takes made here (never an import's), in a fixed order: longest_dictation, fastest_dictation, most_words_day, best_week, longest_meeting, longest_monologue. A best not held yet is absent: nothing to show, never a zero.

week_review.description: Last week, reviewed, to lead the screen with until the user dismisses it (stats.review_dismissed, its week's first day). Absent when last week had no dictation and no meeting, or once dismissed.

MilestonesReached.description: In answer to milestones.check: the milestones reached since the last check, to celebrate, and a best the take just set, for a short note. Each milestone is reported once ever; a library's first check, and any check while stats.celebrate is off, reports none (what is reached is noted all the same). A hidden streak's milestones are noted, not reported.

ref.description: The id of the command this answers, echoed so the shell can match the answer to its question.

milestones.description: The newly reached milestones, in the fixed order of stats.counted's; usually none.

best.description: A best the newest take, today or this week just set: at most one a day, never on a library's first check or with stats.celebrate off, and only once it beat at least five earlier entries. Absent otherwise.

PolishModelState.description: Whether a mode's own language model can polish its takes now: ready (the core holds it, and it sends where it did when the mode was saved), missing (the core does not hold it now: let go of, or another provider chosen; its takes go in as said with polish_model_missing) or moved (it sends somewhere else now than when the mode was saved, such as a custom server re-pointed from this machine to another: its takes go in as said with polish_model_missing until the user confirms it there: modes.save with polish_model_confirm and polish_model_confirm_to, where polish_models says it sends) or unrecorded (where it sends was never recorded, as for a pin saved by an early build: the same until the user confirms it).

ConsentEntry.description: One destination the user agreed a feature may send to.

name.description: For cloud, the provider's name the user agreed to.

endpoint.description: For cloud, its destination: what consent.revoke names to take it away.
